title: Assessment of trachoma in suspected endemic areas in mainland China
author: Jialiang Zhao
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qu9dwz6

steps.title: Select provinces and clusters
steps.instruction: Identify the 14 provinces/autonomous regions to be surveyed (12 historically suspected provinces: Hebei, Inner Mongolia, Liaoning, Anhui, Henan, Hainan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Qinghai, Ningxia; plus Guangxi and Tibet based on lowest GDP/per‑capita income; plus Shandong and Sichuan as pilot areas). Divide each province into 2–3 geographic areas of approximately 100,000–150,000 people using county boundaries and census data, and within each area define suspected endemic zones based on historical literature, recent primary‑school data (last 5 years), and routine eye‑care records.

steps.title: Assemble and train survey teams
steps.instruction: Form 2–3 provincial survey teams per province. Each team consists of a trachoma grader (who also collects ocular swabs), a recorder/assistant, a driver, and a community guide. Include three certified ophthalmologists per provincial team, each equipped with a ×2.5 head‑mounted magnifier, torch, and alcohol‑based hand gel. Conduct a national two‑day structured training in Beijing (WHO officer and international expert), followed by field training in Inner Mongolia, covering the WHO SAFE strategy, TRA methodology, Simplified Grading System, laboratory confirmation, and population identification. Perform inter‑observer agreement testing; all trainees must achieve Cohen’s κ ≥ 0.7 for TF. Then hold provincial‑level training for local ophthalmologists and support staff.

steps.title: Review hospital records
steps.instruction: Visit ophthalmologists in county or leading hospitals of each suspected area. Discuss their knowledge of trachoma, ask about recent TF diagnoses or TT surgeries, and examine hospital records for diagnoses of trachomatous corneal opacity (CO) and TT performed in recent years.

steps.title: Select and examine school children for TF
steps.instruction: In each suspected area, choose at least one primary school (preferably a boarding school with many rural children). Ensure gender balance among participants. At each selected school, examine a minimum of 50 grade‑one children (typically 7 years old) for TF using the WHO Simplified Grading System (≥5 follicles ≥ 0.5 mm on the upper tarsal conjunctiva). Mobilize teachers to encourage participation and reduce bias.

steps.title: Assess TT and CO in villages
steps.instruction: Conduct TT/CO rapid assessment in villages using one of two strategies:

substeps.instruction: If hospital review identified any TT or CO cases, contact those individuals for re‑examination and screen the village(s) where they reside (residents ≥15 years old who have lived there ≥6 months) for additional TT or CO cases.
If no TT or CO records were found, visit at least one village surrounding the school that was examined for TF and screen residents ≥15 years old (≥6 months residence) for TT or CO.

Identify suspected TT/CO cases by consulting village leaders and doctors, then visit the suspect’s home to confirm diagnosis. Mobilize village leaders and doctors as assistants to ensure high inspection coverage and minimise selection bias.

steps.title: Calculate prevalence and decide on population survey
steps.instruction: For each school, compute TF prevalence as the number of TF‑positive children divided by 50 examined. If >4 TF cases are found in any school, plan a population‑based prevalence survey for that area; otherwise, no further survey is needed (no school exceeded two TF cases). For TT and CO, estimate prevalence as confirmed cases divided by the estimated number of persons ≥15 years old in the village.

steps.title: Provide treatment for confirmed cases
steps.instruction: For each TF‑positive child, obtain oral azithromycin from county resources and treat the child with 20 mg kg⁻¹ (or 1 g for adults) as a single dose; also treat all household members. For TT cases, arrange free bilamellar tarsal rotation (or equivalent oculoplastic) surgery at county hospitals. For patients with only one or two inverted eyelashes touching the globe (no entropion), perform electrolysis.

steps.title: Data entry, cleaning and quality control
steps.instruction: Assign a dedicated analyst on each provincial team to record field data, enter it into EpiData 3.0, and review for completeness and accuracy. Follow WHO‑based quality‑control measures: (a) design conforms to WHO TRA and Simplified Grading System; (b) pilot study completed to test feasibility; (c) national and provincial trainings with inter‑observer agreement testing; (d) ongoing supervisory visits by national and international experts throughout field work.
